title: Retry a failed payment
summary: A payment that fails is tried again up to three times before the order is given up.

F6.why: How much a customer should hear about a retry is a promise to your customers, and only you can decide how much to promise.
F6.context: When a payment fails and is tried again, the customer is not told. The retry shows on their card statement as a second charge attempt.

recommendation.reason: The statement line already names the shop.

F7.why: Who tells a customer that their payment could not be taken is a customer-service call, and only you can decide who it comes from and in what words.
F7.context: After the third failed try the order is given up, and nothing is sent. The customer is left on the checkout page with no message.

options.keep-it: Customers whose card keeps failing hear nothing and may think the order went through; support gets the questions.
options.fix-in-a-follow-up: This ships with customers hearing nothing for now; a follow-up adds the email, once you have chosen its wording.
options.fix-before-merge: The PR goes back to have the email written first, and returns with a new sheet; the retry ships later.

recommendation.reason: The email needs wording the owner has not chosen yet.

items.title: Retry for ten minutes after a failure
items.ifLeft: A failed payment is retried for ten minutes, then the order is cancelled.

options.label: Ten minutes
options.consequence: Orders wait up to ten minutes for a payment to clear.

options.label: One minute
options.consequence: The PR goes back to shorten the window and returns with a new sheet.

recommendation.reason: Most card declines clear within that time.

closesSpec.receipt: Every line of the spec's acceptance list has a merged test: retry limit, back-off, order number kept.
